title: Load old ticket rows into states that can't contradict themselves

blocks.text: The help desk's old ticket table has a `status` column (`OPEN`, `ASSIGNED`, `RESOLVED`) and two columns that may be null: `agent` and `resolution`. Years of manual fixes left rows that contradict their status, and the dashboard shows tickets "resolved by null". The new code keeps each ticket as one of three records, `Open`, `Assigned` and `Resolved`, each holding the data of its state.

Finish `src/main/java/practice/Tickets.java`: the two constructors marked `TODO` and `fromRow`. When you're done, no code path, the loader or any other, can produce an `Assigned` without an agent or a `Resolved` without an agent and a resolution (a blank string counts as missing). A row that doesn't fit its status is refused with an `IllegalArgumentException` that lets the data team find the row; nothing in it is silently dropped. `requireText` and `requireEmpty` are there to use. About twenty lines in total.
The tests use their own ticket ids, agents and rows.

cases.says: each consistent row becomes the record its status names, and writing it back gives the same row
a row missing the agent or resolution its status needs, or with an unknown status, is refused
code that builds an Assigned or Resolved directly, without its data, is refused by the record itself
a row whose status can't have an agent or a resolution, but has one, is refused rather than trimmed
a refused row's exception message names the row's id

origin.section: Give Each State Its Own Record, and an Order Without a Tracking Number Can't Be Shipped

concepts: Each state is a record holding only the data true in that state; the compact constructor, not the record itself, refuses a state built without its data.
